minors.name: Acamarians
minors.description: A clan society healing from centuries of blood feuds, with some clans still roaming the stars as raiders. Membership brings their trade networks and a steady flow of credits.

minors.name: Andorians
minors.description: Proud, antennaed warriors from an icy moon and old partners of the Vulcans and humans. Their soldiers harden the ground defenses of every world in the empire they join.

minors.name: Angosians
minors.description: A peaceful society that once engineered its soldiers into living weapons, then struggled to live with them. Their veterans stiffen the defenses of allied worlds.

minors.name: Antedeans
minors.description: Ichthyoid travelers who fall into a stupor aboard starships and rarely trust outsiders. Their ocean harvests add to the food supply of any empire they join.

minors.name: Anticans
minors.description: Carnivorous hunters locked in an ancient feud with the neighboring Selay. Their appetite for battle strengthens the garrisons of any empire they join.

minors.name: Bajorans
minors.description: A deeply spiritual people who endured a brutal occupation with their faith intact. They despise Cardassian rule, and their devotion lifts morale across the empire they join.

minors.name: Bandi
minors.description: Gracious hosts and gifted builders whose showpiece station charmed visitors until its secret came out. Their architects lift industry across any empire they join.

minors.name: Benzites
minors.description: Methodical perfectionists who never solve the same problem twice. Their efficiency experts raise industry throughout the empire they join.

minors.name: Betazoids
minors.description: Telepaths who prize honesty because little can be hidden from them for long. Their counselors ease tension on every world of the empire they join.

minors.name: Bolians
minors.description: Cheerful blue-skinned bankers whose financial houses reach across the quadrant. Membership opens their banks and raises credit income empire-wide.

minors.name: Bynars
minors.description: Paired beings who think in binary and live linked to their planetary computer. Their network adds 10% to the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Caldonians
minors.description: Tall, gentle scholars who value pure research far above commerce. Their think tanks add to the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Chalnoth
minors.description: Anarchist hunters who recognize no authority but strength. If persuaded to join an empire, they make its worlds very costly to invade.

minors.name: Edo
minors.description: A carefree, pleasure-loving people watched over by a powerful guardian entity. Their easygoing culture raises morale across the empire they join.

minors.name: Ktarians
minors.description: Ambitious schemers who once tried to subvert a starship crew with an addictive game. Wary of outsiders, they drive a hard bargain but put industrious hands to work.

minors.name: Malcorians
minors.description: A people on the verge of warp flight who are not yet ready to learn they are not alone. Suspicious of every empire, they bring a busy industrial base to one that wins them over.

minors.name: Mintakans
minors.description: A gentle, rational proto-Vulcan people who once briefly mistook a starship captain for a god. Their communal farms add to the food supply of any empire they join.

minors.name: Mizarians
minors.description: Pacifists who have outlasted repeated conquests by never resisting any of them. Their calm steadies morale in the empire they join.

minors.name: Nausicaans
minors.description: Towering brawlers and hired muscle with a taste for violence. Their young warriors swell the garrisons of any empire that can hold their loyalty.

minors.name: Pakleds
minors.description: Slow-spoken scavengers who acquire technology by trade, trickery or theft. What they collect adds a little to the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Selay
minors.description: Reptilian rivals of the Anticans, just as eager to settle old scores. Their soldiers strengthen the garrisons of any empire they join.

minors.name: Sheliak
minors.description: Legalistic non-humanoids who consider most species barely worth addressing and enforce every clause of every treaty. Their mastery of environments boosts food output empire-wide.

minors.name: Takarans
minors.description: A people whose decentralized bodies shrug off wounds that would kill others. Their curiosity about physical forces adds to the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Talarians
minors.description: A patriarchal military society that treasures its homeworld above all else. Their fortification doctrine makes every world of their empire harder to invade.

minors.name: Tamarians
minors.description: The Children of Tama speak only in metaphors drawn from their myths and history. Once understood, those stories hold insights that raise the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Trill
minors.description: Humanoids who share their lives with long-lived symbionts that carry centuries of memory from host to host. Their joined scientists raise the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Ullians
minors.description: Telepathic historians who collect the memories of other peoples as living archives. Their knowledge adds a little to the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Vulcans
minors.description: Disciples of logic with a scientific tradition older than their warp drive. Vulcan scholars add 15% to the research of any empire they join.

minors.name: Yridians
minors.description: Information dealers who will sell any secret to anyone who can pay. Their brokerage houses raise credit income for any empire they join.

minors.name: Zakdorn
minors.description: Celebrated as the finest strategic minds in the galaxy, though they rarely put the reputation to the test. Their war-planners strengthen the defenses of any empire they join.
